pattern.crimePattern: fired employee kills the bar owner over unpaid wages; an innocent patron lies to hide gambling
pattern.notes: Fictional pub and betting shop. The match on screen is generic: no real teams, kits or competitions named.

ob.reportedBy: Monicah Njeri, waitress, Goal Pub & Screen, Umoja Inner Core
ob.text: Monicah Njeri, a waitress, reports that the owner of Goal Pub & Screen, Umoja Inner Core, Josiah Mutai (56), was found dead in the storeroom at 21:30, at the end of the Sunday match. About sixty customers were in the pub.

people.name: Josiah Mutai
people.bio: Built the pub from a kiosk with one television. Tight with money, loud on match nights.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 50s, heavy-set, short grey hair, a football club-style scarf in plain colours with no badge, a bunch of keys on his belt, loud laugh lines, ID-photo framing

people.name: Ian Kamotho
people.bio: Has run the projector booth for two years. Fired this afternoon; Josiah refused to pay him two months' wages.

image.brief: Kenyan man, late 20s, clean fade haircut, oversized hoodie, a pale band of skin around his neck where headphones usually sit, guarded and very still, ID-photo framing

people.name: Tobias Okoth
people.bio: Shouted at Josiah at half-time over a KSh 300 tab. Says he never left his seat.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 20s, mechanic's overalls tied at the waist over a plain football shirt with no badge, nervous eyes, chewing the inside of his cheek, ID-photo framing

people.name: Purity Chepngetich
people.bio: Inherits the pub. She wanted to sell it; he refused.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, late 40s, church choir robe in maroon over her clothes, hair in a neat wrap, red-eyed and very upright, ID-photo framing

people.name: Monicah Njeri
people.bio: Has waited tables at Goal Pub for four years. Found Josiah when she went for more crates.

people.name: Cynthia Awino
people.bio: Works the live-bet counter across the road. Remembers faces.

people.name: Deacon Samuel Mugambi
people.bio: Keeps the door at the evening service.

places.name: Projector booth beside the storeroom door
Kamari Point betting shop, across the road

locations.name: Goal Pub & Screen, Umoja Inner Core
locations.description: A long room of plastic chairs facing a projector screen. The match is over and the screen shows a frozen replay. Behind the bar, a plywood booth for the screen operator stands right beside the storeroom door.

hotspots.label: Storeroom
hotspots.text: Josiah lies among stacked crates of empties. One crate is split open beside him.

hotspots.label: Behind the crates
hotspots.text: Something black and padded has slipped down behind the stack of crates.

hotspots.label: Projector booth
hotspots.text: A plywood booth with a laptop, a mixer and the projector cable. A painted board over the hatch.

hotspots.label: Note pinned to the bar
hotspots.text: Among the betting tips and phone numbers pinned behind the bar, one note is very angry.

hotspots.label: Waitress at the bar
hotspots.text: Monicah Njeri sits on a bar stool with her tray in her lap.

hotspots.label: Front window
hotspots.text: Across the road, the lights of Kamari Point betting shop are still on, odds scrolling on its screens.

image.brief: inside a busy Nairobi estate bar after a football screening, rows of plastic chairs facing a projector screen showing a frozen generic football pitch with no logos, a plywood projector booth beside a storeroom door, bottles behind the bar, no people in focus

locations.name: Kamari Point betting shop
locations.description: A narrow shop with three screens of scrolling odds and a cashier's window. Slips everywhere on the floor.

hotspots.label: Counter copies
hotspots.text: Cynthia keeps a carbon copy of every live-bet slip, filed by name.

image.brief: a narrow betting shop on a Nairobi estate street at night, screens of scrolling odds, a cashier window with a metal grille, discarded betting slips on the floor

body.note: Report language only. Struck with a crate of empty bottles. Found 21:30.

image.brief: a bar storeroom with crates of empty beer bottles stacked to the ceiling, one crate split open on the floor with bottles spilled, a bare bulb, no body visible

body.label: DJ headphones. Sticker on the band: "DJ KAMO".

image.brief: a pair of black over-ear DJ headphones lying in the gap behind stacked beer crates, a white sticker on the headband reading DJ KAMO

body.text: DJ KAMO on the decks — every Friday & match nights

facts.text: Monicah Njeri found the owner, Josiah Mutai, dead in the storeroom at 21:30, at the end of the match.
Josiah was struck with a crate of empty bottles.
Monicah: at 20:55 Josiah went into the storeroom to count crates.
Monicah: the screen froze for about six minutes in the second half. The pub booed. She went to shout at the booth, and it was empty.
Monicah: Ian ran the screen from the booth all evening, from before kick-off to full time. The booth is right beside the storeroom door.
Monicah served tables the whole second half in front of about sixty customers.
A regular's note: 'FROZE 68'–74''. The second half kicked off at 20:35, so the freeze ran from 20:58 to 21:04.
DJ headphones were lying behind the crates in the storeroom, with a sticker: 'DJ KAMO'.
The board over the booth: 'DJ KAMO on the decks'. DJ Kamo is Ian Kamotho.
Monicah: Josiah fired Ian at three this afternoon and refused him two months' wages. Ian ran the match anyway because there was nobody else.
Monicah: Josiah's wife, Purity, wanted to sell the pub. They fought about it every week.
Monicah: at half-time Tobias Okoth and Josiah shouted at each other over a KSh 300 tab.
Kamari Point counter copies: live bets in the name of Tobias Okoth at 20:48, 20:59 and 21:06, the last for KSh 1,500.
Cynthia: Tobias stood at her counter from about 20:45 to 21:08, watching the odds on the screen.
Cynthia worked the live-bet counter alone from 18:00 to closing; the shop's own camera faces her window.
Deacon Mugambi: Purity sang in the choir from 18:00 until the service ended at 21:30.
Tobias: "I watched the whole second half from my seat. I never left the pub."
Tobias: "Mzee and I shouted about a tab. That's football."
Tobias admits he was at Kamari Point from about 20:45 to 21:08, betting his mother's school-fees money for his sister.
Ian: "I had no problem with Mzee."
Purity: "I was at church until half past nine."
Purity: a buyer offered good money for the pub. Josiah said he would die in it first.

interrogations.intro: Monicah turns her tray over and over. "Sixty people in here, and nobody saw anything. They were all watching the screen."

topics.reply: He was hard, but he paid me. His wife wanted to sell this place. Every week, the same fight.
Mzee fired him at three. No wages for two months. Ian still came and ran the match. I thought, that boy is a saint.
Tobias? He shouted at Mzee at half-time about three hundred bob on his tab. After that I didn't see him. I was busy.

interrogations.intro: Tobias keeps checking his phone, then turning it face down. "I was here. I was watching the match. Like everybody."

topics.reply: Three hundred bob. He said I don't pay. I always pay.

interrogations.intro: Ian sits in his booth with the laptop shut, his hands flat on the lid. "I just play the match."

topics.reply: The stream drops when the Wi-Fi drops. Every match. Ask anyone.
Anyone could have put them there. I leave them everywhere.
He fired me at three. I still ran his match. Does that sound like a man who is angry?

interrogations.intro: Purity has come straight from church in her choir robe. "They called me during the last hymn."

topics.reply: Twenty-three years married. Yes, I wanted to sell. A buyer offered good money. He said he would die in that pub first.
Call the deacon. He keeps the door. He counts us in and out like sheep.

interrogations.intro: Cynthia talks through the grille of her window. "I see a hundred faces a night. Ask me about one."

topics.reply: The mechanic. He stood right here from quarter to nine until after nine, staring at the odds. Second-half bets. The last one was big.

contradictions.reaction: Please. Please don't tell my mother. That was her school-fees money for my sister. I was at Kamari Point the whole time, I swear. Ask the cashier. I lost all of it.

prosecutor.pass: Six minutes of frozen screen, an empty booth beside the storeroom, and his headphones behind the crates. That will hold.
fail: Doesn't hold up. Your liar was across the road losing his mother's money. A lie isn't a killing.
No. Sixty people were looking at one screen. Who was the only person whose job was not to look at it?

proof.concludes: Josiah went into the storeroom at 20:55. From 20:58 to 21:04 the screen froze and the booth beside the storeroom door was empty: the operator left his post exactly when nobody was watching that door.
The operator's headphones, "DJ KAMO", are in the storeroom behind the crates. Ian Kamotho, fired that afternoon and unpaid, killed Josiah.

eliminations.why: Tobias was at the Kamari Point counter from 20:45 to 21:08, placing bets at 20:48, 20:59 and 21:06. His lie hid gambling, not murder.
Purity was singing in the Neema Fellowship choir until 21:30.
Monicah was serving tables in front of sixty customers the whole second half.
Cynthia was alone at her counter across the road, in view of the shop's camera, all evening.

reconstruction.text: 15:00. Josiah fires Ian and refuses two months' wages. "Run tonight's match or get nothing at all."
Half-time. Tobias shouts at Josiah over a KSh 300 tab. At 20:48 he slips across the road to Kamari Point with his mother's school-fees money.
20:55. Josiah goes into the storeroom to count crates. Ian watches the door from his booth.
20:58. Ian lets the stream freeze and walks into the storeroom to ask for his wages. Josiah laughs. Ian swings a crate. His headphones slip off and fall behind the stack.
21:04. Ian is back in the booth. He restarts the stream. Sixty people cheer the picture coming back.

tier1.line: Somebody in that pub was counting minutes. Turn the match minutes into clock times.

tier2.line: The booth was empty while the screen was frozen. Then look behind the crates for something that belongs in the booth.

glossary.def: Respectful word for an older man; here, the owner.

tutorial.line: Some people will not talk until you put something in front of them. Show him what you already know.
A man who lies to you isn't always a man who kills. Find out what he was hiding before you decide what it means.

ui.beatNotes: Broken isn't guilty: after the reaction a broken claim is marked red (the reaction implicates) or grey (the reaction explains). Tobias's goes grey. Also the first guarded suspect: Ian's statement sheet is blank until the player shows him relevant evidence.
